answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a bond that is slashed if it is caught cheating, so spinning up thousands of Sybils costs thousands of bonds. Like a comet, a single fake can flash brightly for a moment, but the juniper root of the system is the locked stake, it stays put through the season. An attacker flooding the canyon of honest agents must pay the toll at every crossing, and losing the bond on detection turns a cheap flood into a costly one.
